# We check if we have an even number of \ in the beginning of	#
			# of the file preceeding an open tag. If we do, then it's		#
			# boilerplate text. We check this in the very beginning because	#
			# if not, the directives/classfeatures etc will match it and we	#
			# won't get the initial backslashes as boilerplate code			#
			(?<boilerplate>^(\\\\)+)(?=<\#)|
			# Check for an unescaped (0 or even number of \ preceeding		#
			# it) directive start tag and it's accompanying end tag. Store	#
			# text of the directive tag in a group named directive			#
			(?<=([^\\]|^)(\\\\)*)<\#@(?<directive>.*?)(?<=[^\\](\\\\)*)\#>|
			# Check for an unescaped classfeature start tag and its end tag	#
			# Store the text between the tags in group called classfeatures	#
			(?<=([^\\]|^)(\\\\)*)<\#\+(?<classfeature>.*?)(?<=[^\\](\\\\)*)\#>|
			# Check for an unescaped expression start tag and its end tag.	#
			# Store the text between the tags in group called expression	#
			(?<=([^\\]|^)(\\\\)*)<\#=(?<expression>.*?)(?<=[^\\](\\\\)*)\#>|
			# Check for an unescaped statement start tag and its end tag.	#
			# Store the text between the tags in group called statement.	#
			# We can only check for statements after checking for			#
			# directives, expressions and classfeatures because the start	#
			# tag for statements is a substring of the other start tags		#
			(?<=([^\\]|^)(\\\\)*)<\#(?<statement>.*?)(?<=[^\\](\\\\)*)\#>|
			# Finally, check for boilerplate code that's not within a start	#
			# or end tag (look for anything preceeding a start tag or an	#
			# EOL) This has to be done at the ver end so that the .+ does	#
			# not match other blocks										#
			(?<boilerplate>.+?)(?=((?<=[^\\](\\\\)*)<\#))|
			(?<boilerplate>.+)(?=$)
